features.metaDescription: Explore ty-plus features: a customizable workspace of preset tiles and widgets inside Adobe After Effects, with local-first storage and release channels.
features.title: Features
features.lead: ty-plus is a CEP extension panel for Adobe After Effects. It gives you a customizable home for the presets and tools you reach for constantly — all running locally inside After Effects.

tiles.title: Your catalog, as a shelf of tiles
tiles.body: Animation presets, code presets, footage, and groups you register become named tiles on the same grid as your widgets — each carrying its own icon and title, all inside After Effects. The stage on the right renders the same tile and info surfaces the panel does.

interaction.title: Inspect, select, apply
interaction.body: Hover or tap a tile and the info surface shows the preset's name, kind, and source — the same readout the panel's info widget renders. ⌘/Ctrl+click toggles a tile in the selection; Shift+click adds to it. A plain click applies the preset to the active layer in After Effects — a path verified end to end against a real project. The demo records that intent as a note rather than simulating the run. The two captures pair the real info widget before and after a selection.
interaction.beforeAlt: The ty-plus info widget in its empty state, reading 'No preset selected'
interaction.beforeCaption: Before — nothing selected: the info widget reads 'No preset selected'.
interaction.afterAlt: The ty-plus info widget listing the selected preset — its name, preset kind, and selection as the source
interaction.afterCaption: After — a tile is selected: the widget lists the preset's name, kind, and 'selection' as its source.

surfaces.title: Widgets and dialogs on the same grid
surfaces.easingAlt: The ty-plus easing widget — a curve editor with Curve, Loop, Bounce, and Elastic modes and an Apply action — beside align and distribute tools
surfaces.easingCaption: The easing curve editor shapes speed curves and applies them to keyframes; align, distribute, and spacing tools sit on the same grid.
surfaces.presetsAlt: The Local Presets browser in ty-plus listing catalog presets with an offline notice
surfaces.presetsCaption: Local Presets — search the catalog and see which workspace holds each preset; browsing keeps working offline.
surfaces.addWidgetAlt: The Add Widget selector in ty-plus listing CORE and UTILITY widget types
surfaces.addWidgetCaption: Add Widget — pick a CORE or UTILITY widget; the dialog states where it lands on the grid.
surfaces.widgetsBody: Easing draws a speed curve you apply to keyframes; Align lines up selected layers and Anchor Point sets the anchor. Directory Browser, Font Viewer, Quick Actions, Menu, Info, and Layout Lock cover the rest. Pick them in Add Widget and they join the same grid as your preset tiles — every widget keeps working with the network unplugged.
surfaces.appearanceBody: Change the workspace background — solid, pattern, or image — from the Menu widget, and tune theme, opacity, and density in Settings. Both are stored in local files on your machine.

availability.title: Offline by design
availability.body: Workspace settings, presets, widget configuration, and appearance live on your machine. The extension checks GitHub Releases for updates, but every core function works without a network connection — and without an account.

steps.title: Three steps to the panel
steps.item1: Download the ZXP for your OS from the release above (or <1>GitHub Releases</1>).
steps.item2: Install the ZXP with a CEP-compatible installer (for example ZXP Installer or Extension Manager).
steps.item3: Restart Adobe After Effects and open <1>Window → Extensions → ty-plus</1>.

download.signingNotice: The Windows native worker is not Authenticode-signed and the macOS worker is not notarized. OS security policies may require adjustments — see the <1>installation and troubleshooting guide</1> for details.

fadeIn.title: Fade In
fadeIn.description: Ramp layer opacity from 0 to 100 over the first 12 frames.

popIn.title: Pop In
popIn.description: Scale the layer up with a soft overshoot, then settle.

slideIn.title: Slide In
slideIn.description: Slide the layer in from off-screen with a gentle ease-out.

jumpIn.title: Jump In
jumpIn.description: Arc the layer into place with a squash on landing.

spinIn.title: Spin In
spinIn.description: Rotate the layer a full turn while fading it in.

fadeOut.title: Fade Out
fadeOut.description: Ramp layer opacity down to 0 over the last 12 frames.

popOut.title: Pop Out
popOut.description: Scale the layer down with a quick ease-in exit.

breathe.title: Breathe Loop
breathe.description: Loop a subtle scale pulse for ambient motion.

yoyo.title: Yo-yo Loop
yoyo.description: Loop position back and forth along one axis.

wobble.title: Pop & Wobble
wobble.description: Overshoot scale, then wobble to rest.

slideOut.title: Slide Out
slideOut.description: Slide the layer off-screen with a soft ease-in.

spinOut.title: Spin Out
spinOut.description: Rotate the layer a full turn while fading it out.
